title: Compact delta-token fallbacks for dim-mode: per-brand contrast tuning and component shims
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: When customers apply branded color palettes in dim/dark console modes we see inconsistent contrast across interactive controls (primary/secondary buttons), table row separators, and chart legends. Existing brand fallback logic maps anchors to a single dark variant which leads to over-darkened accents for some brands and crushed midtones for charts.

Proposal: Introduce a compact set of "delta tokens" that express per-brand contrast adjustments applied on top of the base dark token set. Delta tokens are small signed offsets (lightness/alpha adjustments) that are composable at component boundaries (buttons, table cells, chart legends). Implement component shims for Button, TableRow, ChartLegend that resolve base token -> delta apply -> final CSS token. Keep the global tokens unchanged to preserve backward compatibility for teams that rely on raw values.

Goals: 1) preserve minimum accessible contrast for interactive controls across brand palettes; 2) avoid visual crushing in charts and tables; 3) keep the size of the token set minimal to limit surface area for regressions; 4) enable dynamic theme composition for Dedicated/Private console skins.
acceptance_criteria: Buttons: primary and secondary background/foreground combos meet 4.5:1 AA for large text and 3:1 for non-text icons across 5 example brand palettes
Tables: row hover and selected states maintain clear separation without increasing perceived surface saturation
Charts: legend swatches and axis labels remain distinguishable from background with preserved hue fidelity
Token set size: delta tokens limited to <= 12 new keys for the core console theme
Rollout: feature gated and opt-in per-tenant; fallback to legacy tokens if runtime flag off
tasks: Design: define delta token spec and mapping rules
Engineering: add runtime shim that composes base token + delta in CSS variables
Docs: update token reference and migration guide
QA: visual regressions across 6 brand palettes, automated Percy snapshots
Accessibility: run axe contrast checks and manual keyboard tests
decisions: Use signed delta values (L* and alpha adjustments) rather than discrete named tokens to minimize proliferation
Apply deltas at component surface level (component shim) rather than globally to reduce unintended side-effects
Keep legacy tokens available and behind a runtime feature flag for canary rollouts
tradeoffs: Smaller token set reduces complexity but requires per-component logic which slightly increases runtime CSS composition cost
Signed deltas are compact but harder for designers to reason about vs explicit token names
Per-brand tuning yields best visual results but increases QA matrix size
